THE MEASUREMENT TWO EARLIER FINDINGS SAID WAS OWED, TAKEN 2026-08-31. Both fact:the-decision-race-is-caller-ordering-not-read-after-write (2026-08-09) and fact:the-parallel-batch-class-recurred-because-only-its-instance-was-fixed (2026-08-30) close with the same admission: whether export_graph can in fact be ordered before a write in the same batch is REASONED FROM THE SHARED LOCK, NOT MEASURED. export_graph's tool description had been warning about it on that argument alone. It is now observed.

═══ THE NUMBERS — in-memory backend, 4 worker threads, 200 trials per arm ═══
  ARM A  write CREATES A NODE    91/200 early (~45%)   [repeats: 96, and 79/87 on an earlier cut]
  ARM B  write changes A PROPERTY 10/200 early (~5%)   0 of 10 catchable downstream

Pinned by crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/the_export_can_be_ordered_before_its_writes.rs, ignored by default because these are MEASUREMENTS, not gates — asserting a scheduler outcome is flaky by construction, the same reasoning that made a_dependent_write_in_a_parallel_batch.rs pin the message rather than the race.

⭐ THE METHOD CHANGES THE ANSWER BY 40x, AND THE OBVIOUS METHOD IS THE WRONG ONE. Driving the pair with tokio::join! inside ONE task measures 1%, because join! polls in order and the write almost always takes the lock first. A real MCP server handles each request on ITS OWN TASK; reproduced with tokio::spawn that is 45%. Anyone re-running this must keep the per-task shape — measured the obvious way, this hazard reads as too rare to mention, and the warning already in the description would have looked like overcaution.

🛑 ARM B IS THE FINDING, AND IT IS THE SHAPE THE FIELD REPORT CARRIED. sync_debt raises its unexported-work nudge on live_nodes > export_nodes — A NODE COUNT (crates/reflow2-mcp/src/sync_debt.rs:181). A write that only changes a PROPERTY moves no count, so an early export holding the OLD value is byte-indistinguishable to that check from a complete one. Measured: 0 of 10 early exports would have been caught. Alex's 2026-08-30 report was exactly this — set_artifact_checksum, a property write, and an export that still carried the old checksum. The net that exists would not have told him, and the design should stop implying it would.

═══ WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH ═══
· IN-MEMORY BACKEND ONLY. The RocksDB backend holds the same lock so the mechanism should carry, but the rates are not measured there and a slower write would move them.
· NOT MEASURED THROUGH A REAL MCP TRANSPORT. These call the service methods directly; a client's own batching may interleave differently.
· ARM B's ~5% is NOT established as the general property-write rate. That arm seeds a node first, so the extra sequenced write warms the lock and the scheduler, and the seeding is a confound rather than a control. What is established is that the shape occurs and that nothing downstream sees it.
· WHETHER TO BUILD A DETECTOR IS NOT DECIDED HERE. A completeness check that moved on ANY write rather than on node count would close it — the service already counts write generations at service.rs write_gen — but that counter is per-process and resets on restart, so it is a candidate, not a design.
